about.title: Dana Point Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Dana Point's harbor-town streets carry heavy weekend and commuter traffic where Pacific Coast Highway meets Stonehill Drive and the I-5 corridor, and public crash records show dozens of injury collisions here each year, with Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. showing the most reports. Whether you were rear-ended near the harbor exits, sideswiped merging onto the freeway, or hit at a Route 1 intersection, the aftermath usually means medical appointments, missed work, and calls from an insurance adjuster who wants a quick recorded statement. We handle California personal injury cases and can review your situation and explain your options. There's no charge to speak with us, and we only get paid if you recover compensation. Getting the right information early, before evidence disappears or memories fade, can matter more than people expect.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Talking to the Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury lawsuit in California, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government entity — like a city road crew or public bus — was involved. We can flag deadlines early so evidence isn't lost while you wait.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Cut Your Recovery
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning even if you're found partly responsible, you can still recover damages reduced by your share of fault. Insurers often use recorded statements to inflate that percentage, which is why it helps to have guidance before you speak with them.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering, No Fee Unless You Recover
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in a typical car accident case, and we work on contingency — you owe nothing upfront and nothing at all unless there's a recovery.

items.question: I was hit near the Stonehill Drive and PCH area — does it matter exactly where the crash happened?
items.answer: Location can matter for identifying witnesses, traffic camera footage, or nearby businesses with security video, especially along busy corridors like Pacific Coast Highway or the I-5 interchange. We can help figure out what evidence might still be available near the specific site of your crash. Acting sooner rather than later gives you a better shot at preserving that information.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company already called me — should I give them a recorded statement?
items.answer: You're generally not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and doing so before speaking with an attorney can sometimes work against you. Adjusters may use your own words to shift blame under California's comparative fault rules. It's usually safer to speak with an independent attorney first.

items.question: What does it cost to get a case review?
items.answer: Nothing. We offer a free case review — there's no charge to speak with us. If you decide to move forward, we work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if your case results in a recovery.
